appraisal_events.evidence: "puisque j'étais tout et que vous n'étiez rien, c'est moi qui ai fait les premiers pas vers vous"; he calls the narrator's response sottish, accuses him of failing his test of amiability, of spreading "inventions calomniatrices," and declares "l'entretien... marquera pour nos relations le point final" / "nous ne nous connaîtrons plus."
appraisal_events.explanation: Charlus delivers a long tirade of scorn and reproach, casting the narrator as ignorant, ungrateful, and beneath him, then formally terminates their relation; the narrator's own framing of Charlus's theatrical self-pity and grandiosity keeps the reader from taking the charge at face value even as it lands on the narrator within the scene.

appraisal_events.evidence: "un jus olivâtre, hépatique, semblait prêt à sortir de sa bouche mauvaise"; "cet homme était capable d'assassiner et de prouver à force de logique et de beau langage qu'il avait eu raison de le faire"
appraisal_events.explanation: In an aside during Charlus's tirade, the narrator paints him in grotesque, morally damning terms; the acknowledgment of his superior intelligence does not offset the dominant note of physical and moral repugnance.

status_effects.explanation: Charlus repeatedly casts the narrator as ignorant, discourteous, and a source of calumny, locally lowering his standing in the exchange.
Charlus formally ends their relation ("le point final," "nous ne nous connaîtrons plus"), excluding the narrator from his favor after having claimed to have made an exceptional overture.
The narrator's grotesque physical description and characterization of Charlus as capable of murder-with-eloquent-justification diminish him even while granting his intelligence and rank.

ambiguities: Charlus's blame is staged as wounded magnanimity, but the narrator's surrounding irony (the grotesque portrait, the mocking "etc., etc.") undercuts his claimed authority to judge, so it is uncertain how far the passage endorses the substance of his accusations even though their social effect on the narrator is plain.
